A human with Cloudflare dashboard/API access MUST run the plan workflow (.github/workflows/cloudflare-zone-plan.yml) and review every reported diff line before the apply workflow is ever run for the first time. Do not assume any single field here is correct.
_meta.sharedZoneWarning: The Cloudflare zone is the apex domain j172.tw, shared with bid.j172.tw on the same hosting account (see docs/domains/11-hosting-ops-incidents.md). All zone-level settings, Cache Rules, WAF custom rules, rate limiting rules, and Transform Rules in this file apply to the WHOLE zone unless their `expression` scopes them to a specific host. The source documents this file was built from (docs/archive/CLOUDFLARE_OPTIMIZATION.md) use a generic `yourdomain.com` placeholder and do not show host-scoping — it is unconfirmed whether the live rules are scoped to `health.j172.tw` or apply zone-wide (and therefore also to bid.j172.tw). Resolve this during the first plan review, before any apply.

tieredCache.note: Confirmed enabled via .github/workflows/cloudflare-config.yml (shipped before this file existed). This is the one setting in this file that has actually been applied through a version-controlled workflow.

crawlerHints.note: Dashboard-managed, NOT read or written by the plan/apply scripts: Cloudflare has no documented, stable public REST API for Crawler Hints (confirmed 2026-10-12 during issue #454 — the only known endpoint is an undocumented internal flags call, and calling it from cloudflare-zone-plan.mjs caused a live HTTP 400). docs/2.0/spec-issue-438.md §T lists turning this ON as a still-pending 2.0 action item (to let it replace the site's self-written IndexNow submission code); `enabled` here records the intended target state for a human to set manually via Caching > Configuration in the dashboard, not a value this tooling enforces.

botManagement.note: issue #455 (2.0 §T): allows all 3 AI-crawler categories (Search/Agent/Training — Cloudflare API fields ai_search/ai_user/ai_training, confirmed free-plan-available per the 2026-07-01 changelog). 'disabled' means NOT blocked for that category, on every field including the legacy aiBotsProtection toggle — set to 'disabled' too (not left at its old 'block' value) because Cloudflare's docs say the 3 category fields 'replace' that single toggle, and leaving it at 'block' risked an ambiguous conflicting legacy rule still blocking the exact bots this change means to allow. Before this change: fight_mode=true and ai_bots_protection=block, corroborated by memory (ops_cloudflare_bot_protection.md: both turned ON 2026-08-16) and a 2026-10-12 live test (GPTBot/ClaudeBot got 403, PerplexityBot got 200). This unblock MUST ship in the same change as: (1) the cache rules below actually being live (html/llms.txt/.md eligible for edge cache, so crawler traffic mostly hits Cloudflare's cache instead of the origin), (2) the new health-repo:limit-bot-traffic rate-limiting rule below, and (3) the documented SemrushBot/AhrefsBot WAF block (see documentedUnmanagedRules) surviving untouched — see docs/2.0/spec-issue-438.md §T item 348's explicit load-risk note (AI crawler traffic previously worsened an NPROC-exhaustion incident, which is why ai_bots_protection was turned to block on 2026-08-16 in the first place). Monitoring plan: compare host NPROC + Cloudflare cache hit rate daily for 72h after apply (recorded in issue #455's comments); if NPROC alerts reappear, revert ONLY aiTraining back to 'block' and leave aiSearch/aiUser as 'disabled' (allowed). crawlerProtection=null remains genuinely unconfirmed (unrelated to this change) — confirmed 2026-10-12 via issue #454's first live plan run that the real zone has it set to 'enabled'; the plan/apply scripts deliberately skip diffing/writing this field while it's null.

cacheRules.description: Bypass Cache for Admin & Admin APIs
Respect Origin for Public HTML & SWR

wafCustomRules.expression: (starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/admin") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/api/admin")) and (cf.threat_score gt 0 or not ip.src.country in {"TW"})

rateLimitingRules.note: issue #455's required mitigation paired with allowing AI crawlers (2.0 §T item 348): throttles verified-bot traffic specifically, zone-wide, so a single crawler cannot hammer the origin at a rate the host's known LVE process ceiling can't absorb (see ops_health_502_watchdog memory notes on prior NPROC-exhaustion incidents). cf.client.bot (free-plan-available, confirmed via Cloudflare's ruleset-engine field reference docs) flags known-good bots/crawlers, which is exactly the traffic class this unblock adds, without touching real browser visitors. action is 'block' rather than 'managed_challenge'/'js_challenge': those challenge types require solving a JS challenge, which a legitimate crawler cannot do, so challenging bot traffic would silently defeat the entire point of allowing it — 'block' instead just rejects requests over the limit outright (a clean, bot-interpretable backoff signal) without demanding JS execution.

documentedUnmanagedRules.description: Blocks SemrushBot and AhrefsBot (exact expression text not available in this repo's docs)
documentedUnmanagedRules.note: Called out explicitly in docs/2.0/spec-issue-438.md §T as a rule that MUST survive the config-as-code import ('設定即程式碼匯入時不得遺失'). This repo intentionally does NOT manage this rule's content — the plan/apply tooling treats any live rule not tagged with a health-repo:* ref as unmanaged and never rewrites or drops it when it updates the http_request_firewall_custom ruleset. This entry exists purely so the rule's existence and intent are documented in version control, not to control its content. Verify the live rule ID still matches on first plan run.
